# Timbaland Announces Partnership with AI-Music Start-up Suno (Rolling Stone)

By Brian Hiatt. Published October 22, 2024.

## Key findings
- Timbaland joined **Suno** as a **creative advisor** and announced a remix contest.
- He had become obsessed with Suno's "cover songs" beta feature (upload your own audio, have the software extend and reimagine it), spending **more than ten hours a day** reworking beats from his archive by typing prompts.
- He nicknamed the Suno interface "Baby Timbo."
- He insists musicians shouldn't worry about being supplanted: his process requires human-created audio to start. "You still need that human element to operate this tool. It doesn't replace anything. All it does is add to your arsenal."
- Remix contest: users could use Suno to remix an entirely human-created Timbaland track, "Love Again," with "over $100k in prizes."
- Suno CEO **Mikey Shulman**: "Our team was blown away to learn that Timbaland was a Suno power user... He has already inspired so many people to make music in innovative ways."

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — Rolling Stone, top-tier; first-hand.
- Establishes the Timbaland–Suno creative-adviser partnership (Oct 2024) and his heavy, human-in-the-loop use of Suno in his own production. This is the basis for classifying Timbaland as a human artist who actively uses AI in his music.
